questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead is now divided. Keep to the right of the divider.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn or U-turn at your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign marks reserved parking spaces for vehicles with a handicap sticker, tag, or license plate.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection if it is clear. You can turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: What should you know when approaching a heavy truck from behind on a hill?

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. You cannot safely or legally pass on hills with limited visibility.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This orange construction sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what is the safest way to get home?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest option is to ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce the effects of alcohol. The body takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for road hazards. This sign tells you a sharp turn is coming. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull to the side of the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut off the driver in return.

questions.explanation: Do not react to aggressive driving. Ignore it and keep driving safely. This prevents road rage and keeps you and others safe.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they drive more carefully.
They react faster than sober drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that your car will be towed if you park in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will be very slippery when it rains.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are going through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicycle.
When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others who do not see you. For example, honk if a child is running into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they can do from a specific lane at an intersection. You can either turn left or continue straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn you about work zones. This sign tells you a flagger is ahead. Follow their directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided red signs mean you must stop. Look for traffic and yield the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
Certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Drivers in both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This sign marks an HOV (high occupancy vehicle) lane. HOV lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver and at least one passenger, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Should you signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving the curb?

options.text: Only if other traffic is present.
Yes, it is good practice and the law requires it.
Only during the move, not before.
No, not if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is good practice and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving left or right. Always signal before leaving the curb to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs and alcohol together?

options.text: It increases the chance of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm your brain and make driving unsafe. Mixing alcohol with drugs greatly increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road joins from the right.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Speed up to cross faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell drivers that a train might be near. Always obey these signs and barriers. Never go around lowered gates.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand in traffic lanes where another car could hit you. Turn off the engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Why should you be extra careful around a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction. You may cross only to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Always be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when pulling from a parking space into traffic, moving into a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give way to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You can continue, but drive at a speed where you can slow down and stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules drivers must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It stops other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Leave plenty of space around your car to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do when facing an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance from the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When should you always signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or lot. Signals tell other drivers what you are doing and help prevent crashes.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces focus. Wait to drive if you are upset.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of their way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up as they try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of their way.
questions.explanation: Move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may anger them more and make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you check?

options.text: Only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Only children have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: Which of these distractions increases crash risk?
questions.explanation: Cell phones (even hands-free), radios, and CD players distract you from driving and increase crash risk.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Protecting yourself from bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the bridge or overpass ahead is low. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are coming.

questions.explanation: This sign (with the arrow below) marks where bicycles cross or ride next to traffic. Drive slowly and watch for bicycles in this area.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway with multiple lanes and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, you must slow down, clear the path for the emergency vehicle, and stop. Do not try to speed ahead of the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway changes to the right ahead.
Hiking trails are to the right ahead.
A hotel is to the right ahead.
A hospital is to the right ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hospital is to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your original lane.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a defect that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed right away. Fix defects before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When you are about to change lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: When alcohol and another drug are used together, the effects of both can become much stronger. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.
